:::{#def-design-matrix}
#### Design matrix, model matrix

In a regression model with $n$ observations and $p$ predictors,
the **design matrix**
[@wikipedia_design_matrix]
(or **model matrix**) $\mX$
is the $n \times p$ matrix whose $i$-th row $\tp{\vx_i}$ holds,
for observation $i$,
the values of the $p$ explanatory variables the model uses.
These can be covariates, a constant $1$ for the intercept,
indicator (dummy) variables for categories,
or values computed from covariates, such as $x^2$.
For a straight-line fit, for example, the first column is all 1s,
which allows the intercept to be estimated [@wikipedia_design_matrix; @dobson4e, Section 2.4].
In symbols,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mX
&=
\begin{bmatrix}
\tp{\vx_1} \\
\tp{\vx_2} \\
\vdots \\
\tp{\vx_n}
\end{bmatrix} \\
&=
\begin{bmatrix}
x_{11} & x_{12} & \cdots & x_{1p} \\
x_{21} & x_{22} & \cdots & x_{2p} \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
x_{n1} & x_{n2} & \cdots & x_{np}
\end{bmatrix}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
